title: Bringing Bunk Johnson to Kansas City
summary: Ellis Burton wanted a New Orleans attraction, so Price suggested Bunk Johnson, who arrived too high to play and was sent home.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. Now, let's see. Abe Bowler , you know, the bass player. Abe was in Kansas City. 'Cause Abe was with the Blue Devils too, you know. And...
You worked with Bunk Johnson in Kansas City...

Let me tell you, Ellis Burden asked me who we could get from New Orleans, you know, that...just to have around because... the music wasn't important, you see. He had a gambling house. See..these...it's just like a gambling house...and having the music, that's just a come-on for people to come, and the man to bring his lady, and she'll listen to the music and he'll go back and gamble. Same way as we talked about a record...making records...having a record store. Well, you get your shoes shined and you hear a record and you buy it. So that's the way that was.
Let's see now...what did I say...
Why did he want to get somebody from New Orleans?
Well, as an attraction, you know. People, you know... well, Sammy Price from Texas, slick dude, you know, smart and you know, know a lot of people, he's popular. You know,

because people come in, buy drinks and gamble and all that, and so he said...I suggested that we get Bunk Johnson. Well, we got Bunk Johnson and by the time that he got there he was so darn high that he didn't know where he was. I don't think Bunk even remembered even coming to Kansas City. 'Cause he stayed around there two or three days and we couldn't do anything with him at all. So we sent him back to New Orleans. He tried to play, but he couldn't play. And lost his cap and you know and all that business. But he couldn't play. He came to Kansas City with the intention of playing, but he didn't quite accomplish his mission.
